decisions.reason: As a space navigation and observation camera closely tied to our core optical and guidance capabilities, it remains a product we can improve and support effectively through our strong in-house R&D and accumulated mission knowledge.

The modular navigation camera line fits our established competence base especially well and its platform character across several models gives us strong scope to learn, adapt, and reuse existing components and know-how.

The miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR sensor matches our strategic move toward compact spacecraft instruments, but its weaker market visibility still implies a somewhat higher risk if commercial uptake or qualification progress disappoints.

A radiation-hard space camera line is very close to our core space-imaging expertise and, with several models and dedicated presentation, it appears well positioned for further refinement rather than withdrawal.

The asteroid navigation and imaging camera builds on our established optical-navigation knowledge and offers learning value for future missions, though its narrower application niche and lighter website presence make it less secure than our main platform products.
